## In the MRP

The parameter $s̄$ represents fiscal capacity. It is the highest five-year average primary balance as a share of gross domestic product in the country's own history. Data comes from the International Monetary Fund World Economic Outlook and Fiscal Monitor. This figure shows the surplus the country has demonstrated it can sustain. The parameter $s_t$ is the current-year projected primary balance. Soft information, such as institutional quality or restructuring history, may place $s̄$ below this historical estimate. It never places it above the demonstrated maximum. Sensitivity grids typically show $s̄$ to be the most consequential input.

## In the DAP

The discretionary adjustments process assesses fiscal capacity under task C3*. Teams look for three types of issues. C3-E applies when the estimator fails or rests on one episode. Red flags include never having a five-year surplus or relying on one exceptional pre-crisis window. Teams use realism benchmarks or the euro-area median as fallbacks. C3-T applies when history lags policy. Red flags include adopted consolidation or expansion plans and binding corrective paths under the EU fiscal framework. C3-A applies when default is chosen, not just suffered. Red flags include mainstream platforms normalizing restructuring, a collapse of the consolidation consensus, or sustained government instability at high debt.

## Methods by Document Type

### [Country Report](../document-types/country-report.qmd)

- The [European Commission](../institutions/european-commission.qmd) assesses fiscal capacity based on the general government balance, primary balance, and structural adjustments. It references the Spring 2026 forecast for deficit projections. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/country-reports/Croatia_2026-06-03, p. 42" aria-label="Source: ec/country-reports/Croatia_2026-06-03, p. 42">ⓘ</button>
- The document details general government balance, primary balance targets, tax revenue structures, and spending compositions to evaluate fiscal space and capacity. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/country-reports/Bulgaria_2026-06-03, p. 6, p. 15" aria-label="Source: ec/country-reports/Bulgaria_2026-06-03, p. 6, p. 15">ⓘ</button>
- The [European Commission](../institutions/european-commission.qmd) assesses fiscal capacity based on the general government balance and debt sustainability. It notes whether a country has robust public finances and fiscal space to address challenges. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/country-reports/Cyprus_2026-06-03, p. 4" aria-label="Source: ec/country-reports/Cyprus_2026-06-03, p. 4">ⓘ</button>
- The [European Commission](../institutions/european-commission.qmd) assesses fiscal capacity through the medium-term fiscal-structural plan. It targets a deficit below 3% of gross domestic product by 2028 and monitors compliance via the excessive deficit procedure. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/country-reports/Austria_2026-06-03, p. 37" aria-label="Source: ec/country-reports/Austria_2026-06-03, p. 37">ⓘ</button>
- The document analyzes fiscal capacity through the lens of the medium-term fiscal structural plan, assessing the plausibility of the projected primary balance improvements. It notes that while the plan commits to consolidation, the actual implementation and effectiveness of measures remain to be seen. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/country-reports/Belgium_2026-06-03, p. 3" aria-label="Source: ec/country-reports/Belgium_2026-06-03, p. 3">ⓘ</button>
- The document relies on the [European Commission](../institutions/european-commission.qmd) Spring 2026 Forecast for projections of the general government deficit and debt. It assesses fiscal capacity through the lens of the new national fiscal framework (debt anchor of 40% of GDP) and the extended adjustment period under the EU fiscal rules. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/country-reports/Finland_2026-06-03, p. 5" aria-label="Source: ec/country-reports/Finland_2026-06-03, p. 5">ⓘ</button>
- The Commission’s debt sustainability analysis indicates high fiscal sustainability risks in the medium term for France. The assessment relies on the government’s medium-term fiscal-structural plan and compliance with EU fiscal framework rules. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/country-reports/France_2026-06-03, p. 5" aria-label="Source: ec/country-reports/France_2026-06-03, p. 5">ⓘ</button>
- Fiscal projections are based on the medium-term fiscal-structural plan (MTP) and the Commission Spring 2026 Forecast. The primary balance improvement is discussed in the context of the MTP's commitment to limit net expenditure growth until 2029. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/country-reports/Germany_2026-06-03, p. 7, p. 40" aria-label="Source: ec/country-reports/Germany_2026-06-03, p. 7, p. 40">ⓘ</button>
- The document reports the general government balance and primary surplus as percentages of gross domestic product. It highlights the primary surplus as a key indicator of fiscal capacity, noting it remains above 3.5% of gross domestic product. The impact of adopted consolidation measures (tax cuts, social spending) and defense expenditure increases on the fiscal balance is analyzed. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/country-reports/Greece_2026-06-03, p. 5-6, p. 36-37" aria-label="Source: ec/country-reports/Greece_2026-06-03, p. 5-6, p. 36-37">ⓘ</button>
- The report relies on the [European Commission](../institutions/european-commission.qmd) Spring 2026 Forecast for deficit and debt projections. It analyzes the primary balance and the impact of stock-flow adjustments. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/country-reports/Italy_2026-06-03, p. 47" aria-label="Source: ec/country-reports/Italy_2026-06-03, p. 47">ⓘ</button>
- The document reports primary balance proxies via general government deficit and debt ratios. It details the impact of defence spending and tax reforms on fiscal sustainability. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/country-reports/Latvia_2026-06-03, p. 3" aria-label="Source: ec/country-reports/Latvia_2026-06-03, p. 3">ⓘ</button>
- The European Commission assesses fiscal position using both standard GDP-based metrics and GNI*-adjusted metrics. It highlights the distortion caused by windfall corporate taxes in headline budget figures. The primary balance is implied by the general government surplus given the low debt stock. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/country-reports/Ireland_2026-06-03, p. 3, p. 31" aria-label="Source: ec/country-reports/Ireland_2026-06-03, p. 3, p. 31">ⓘ</button>
- Fiscal projections incorporate the national escape clause for defence spending and tax reforms. The primary balance is implied by the general government balance and interest expenditure. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/country-reports/Lithuania_2026-06-03, p. 4, p. 39" aria-label="Source: ec/country-reports/Lithuania_2026-06-03, p. 4, p. 39">ⓘ</button>
- The document relies on the European Commission’s Spring 2026 Forecast for general government balance, primary balance implications (via primary spending evolution), and debt sustainability analysis based on the country’s medium-term fiscal-structural plan endorsed by the Council. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/country-reports/Luxembourg_2026-06-03, pp. 5, 37" aria-label="Source: ec/country-reports/Luxembourg_2026-06-03, pp. 5, 37">ⓘ</button>
- The report details general government deficit and debt projections, as well as primary balance components implied by deficit and interest expenditure. It discusses fiscal governance, including the role of independent fiscal institutions. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/country-reports/Netherlands_2026-06-03, p. 33, p. 39" aria-label="Source: ec/country-reports/Netherlands_2026-06-03, p. 33, p. 39">ⓘ</button>
- The document provides data on general government balance, structural primary balance, and debt-to-GDP ratios, which are critical for assessing fiscal capacity and debt sustainability. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/country-reports/Malta_2026-06-03, p. 4, p. 35" aria-label="Source: ec/country-reports/Malta_2026-06-03, p. 4, p. 35">ⓘ</button>
- Fiscal projections are based on the [European Commission](../institutions/european-commission.qmd)'s Spring 2026 economic forecast, incorporating the medium-term fiscal-structural plan and assumed policy measures. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/country-reports/Portugal_2026-06-03, p. 5, p. 41" aria-label="Source: ec/country-reports/Portugal_2026-06-03, p. 5, p. 41">ⓘ</button>
- Fiscal projections are based on the medium-term fiscal-structural plan adopted by Slovenia, which includes measures to contain current expenditure and implement structural reforms. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/country-reports/Slovenia_2026-06-03, p. 5" aria-label="Source: ec/country-reports/Slovenia_2026-06-03, p. 5">ⓘ</button>
- The analysis focuses on the best five-year average primary balance and current-year projected primary balance. The document highlights the need for significant fiscal consolidation to meet EU targets, noting the absence of a comprehensive long-term fiscal strategy. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/country-reports/Slovakia_2026-06-03, p. 4, p. 5" aria-label="Source: ec/country-reports/Slovakia_2026-06-03, p. 4, p. 5">ⓘ</button>
- Fiscal assessments are based on the general government deficit and debt-to-GDP ratios, along with the medium-term fiscal structural plan (MTFSP). - The document references the "fiscal stance" as a measure of the annual change in the underlying budgetary position, defined as the difference between medium-term potential growth and the change in primary expenditure net of discretionary revenue measures, including EU-funded expenditure. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/recommendations/Austria_2026-06-03, p. 4" aria-label="Source: ec/recommendations/Austria_2026-06-03, p. 4">ⓘ</button>

- Fiscal assessments are based on the general government deficit, debt-to-GDP ratios, and net expenditure ceilings set by the [Council of the EU](../institutions/council-of-the-eu.qmd). The document notes deviations from these ceilings but emphasizes the position in surplus. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/recommendations/Cyprus_2026-06-03, p. 5" aria-label="Source: ec/recommendations/Cyprus_2026-06-03, p. 5">ⓘ</button>
- The document relies on the [European Commission](../institutions/european-commission.qmd) Spring 2026 Forecast for projections of general government balance, primary surplus, and debt-to-GDP ratios. It uses Eurostat data for historical actuals. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/recommendations/Cyprus_2026-06-03, p. 4" aria-label="Source: ec/recommendations/Cyprus_2026-06-03, p. 4">ⓘ</button>
- The [European Commission](../institutions/european-commission.qmd) assessed effective action under the excessive deficit procedure and evaluated compliance with net expenditure limits while implementing structural reforms. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/recommendations/Belgium_2026-06-03, p. 4, p. 6" aria-label="Source: ec/recommendations/Belgium_2026-06-03, p. 4, p. 6">ⓘ</button>
- The document uses the Commission Spring 2026 Forecast for deficit and debt projections, incorporating known policy measures up to the cut-off date. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/recommendations/Bulgaria_2026-06-03, p. 4" aria-label="Source: ec/recommendations/Bulgaria_2026-06-03, p. 4">ⓘ</button>
- The [European Commission](../institutions/european-commission.qmd) uses the concept of "net expenditure" and its growth rate to monitor compliance with the EU fiscal framework. The "fiscal stance" is defined as the annual change in the underlying budgetary position, measured as the difference between medium-term potential growth and the change in primary expenditure net of discretionary revenue measures. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/recommendations/Germany_2026-06-03, p. 4" aria-label="Source: ec/recommendations/Germany_2026-06-03, p. 4">ⓘ</button>
- The document assesses fiscal capacity through the lens of the EU fiscal framework, using net expenditure growth rates, structural plans, and the definition of fiscal stance as the change in primary expenditure net of discretionary revenue measures. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/recommendations/Greece_2026-06-03, p. 5–6" aria-label="Source: ec/recommendations/Greece_2026-06-03, p. 5–6">ⓘ</button>
- The document uses the Commission Spring 2026 Forecast to project general government balance and debt, based on policy measures known at the cut-off date. It assesses fiscal stance based on primary expenditure changes net of discretionary revenue measures. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/recommendations/Ireland_2026-06-03, p. 4-5" aria-label="Source: ec/recommendations/Ireland_2026-06-03, p. 4-5">ⓘ</button>
- The document assesses fiscal sustainability risks and the alignment of the budget with the corrective path under the excessive deficit procedure, focusing on net expenditure growth rates and the primary balance implied by the deficit and interest costs. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/recommendations/France_2026-06-03, p. 5-6" aria-label="Source: ec/recommendations/France_2026-06-03, p. 5-6">ⓘ</button>
- The document defines the fiscal stance as a measure of the annual change in the underlying budgetary position, including nationally and EU-financed expenditure. It is measured as the difference between medium-term potential growth and the change in primary expenditure net of discretionary revenue measures. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/recommendations/Malta_2026-06-03, p. 4" aria-label="Source: ec/recommendations/Malta_2026-06-03, p. 4">ⓘ</button>
- The [European Commission](../institutions/european-commission.qmd) assesses the fiscal stance and net expenditure growth against recommended maximum rates under the EU fiscal framework (Regulation (EU) 2024/1263). ### [Debt Sustainability Monitor](../document-types/debt-sustainability-monitor.qmd)

- The document uses a no-fiscal-policy-change baseline from 2027 onwards, anchoring the structural primary balance to the 2026 forecast. This implies that any adjustment committed in medium-term plans beyond 2026 is not included in the baseline projection. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 122" aria-label="Source: ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 122">ⓘ</button>
- The baseline assumes the structural primary balance remains constant at its 2026 forecast level until 2036, except for ageing costs. Alternative scenarios include a convergence to historical average SPB and a lower SPB scenario. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 28, p. 43" aria-label="Source: ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 28, p. 43">ⓘ</button>
- The long-term fiscal sustainability indicators S1 and S2 measure the required fiscal effort. S2 is the immediate and permanent one-off change in the structural primary balance needed to stabilize public debt over an infinite horizon. S1 is the change needed to bring debt to 60% of GDP by 2070. Risk categories are assigned based on the size of these adjustments (low if <2% of GDP, medium if 2-6%, high if >6%). <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 283-289" aria-label="Source: ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 283-289">ⓘ</button>
- The document employs stochastic projections with 10,000 shocks to assess uncertainty, covering 80% of simulated debt paths. Deterministic stress tests include scenarios for adverse interest-growth differentials, lower SPB, historical SPB, and financial stress. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 122" aria-label="Source: ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 122">ⓘ</button>

### [Economic Forecast](../document-types/economic-forecast.qmd)

- The forecast highlights significant fiscal pressure due to defense investments and rising public debt for [Finland](../countries/finland.qmd). <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/forecast/Spring-2026-Economic-Forecast_2026-05-21, p. 148" aria-label="Source: ec/forecast/Spring-2026-Economic-Forecast_2026-05-21, p. 148">ⓘ</button>
- For [Sweden](../countries/sweden.qmd), the general government deficit widens significantly due to tax cuts and increased defense spending. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/forecast/Spring-2026-Economic-Forecast_2026-05-21, p. 162" aria-label="Source: ec/forecast/Spring-2026-Economic-Forecast_2026-05-21, p. 162">ⓘ</button>

### [Economic Survey](../document-types/economic-survey.qmd)

- Long-run fiscal projections assume current tax and spending policies unless specified otherwise. The "Consolidation scenario" assumes the primary budget surplus reaches 0.6% of GDP by 2030. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Belgium_2024-09-23, p. 40" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Belgium_2024-09-23, p. 40">ⓘ</button>
- The [OECD](../institutions/oecd.qmd) assesses fiscal capacity using the structural primary balance, adjusted for the output gap and one-off measures. The analysis includes long-term projections of ageing-related expenditures. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Austria_2026-03-19, p. 29" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Austria_2026-03-19, p. 29">ⓘ</button>
- The OECD projects that without policy adjustments, the government debt ratio (Maastricht definition) would rise to 160% by 2060 due to current budget deficits and ageing pressures. A consolidation scenario assumes an improvement in the primary fiscal balance by 0.5% of GDP per year over 2027-2033. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Bulgaria_2026-02-05, p. 54" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Bulgaria_2026-02-05, p. 54">ⓘ</button>
- The [OECD](../institutions/oecd.qmd) estimates the structural deficit and projects the general government fiscal balance based on policy assumptions, including the impact of recent tax changes and defense spending increases. The underlying government primary balance is used as a key indicator of fiscal effort. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Finland_2025-05-23, p. 22" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Finland_2025-05-23, p. 22">ⓘ</button>
- The [OECD](../institutions/oecd.qmd) conducts simulations using the [OECD](../institutions/oecd.qmd) Long-term Model to assess fiscal sustainability. Issuing public debt to finance additional defence and infrastructure spending, while using the structural deficit limit, would increase the debt-to-GDP ratio to about 81% by 2045. If rising spending pressures due to ageing are not addressed, debt would increase to about 128% of GDP in 2045. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Germany_2025-06-12, p. 38-39" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Germany_2025-06-12, p. 38-39">ⓘ</button>
- Fiscal sustainability is assessed using stylized debt scenarios. The "Current policies" scenario projects debt rising to 90% of GDP by 2040. The "Fiscal rules scenario" assumes a structural primary budget deficit of 0.4% is reached in 2028, stabilizing debt at around 55% of GDP. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Croatia_2026-01-30, p. 24" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Croatia_2026-01-30, p. 24">ⓘ</button>
- The analysis relies on [OECD](../institutions/oecd.qmd) Long-Term Model simulations and [European Commission](../institutions/european-commission.qmd) ageing projections to assess debt sustainability and the impact of structural reforms on the primary balance. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/France_2026-06-30, p. 27" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/France_2026-06-30, p. 27">ⓘ</button>
- The document analyzes primary balance projections and debt sustainability scenarios, assuming primary surpluses of around 2% of GDP. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Greece_2024-12-05, p. 35" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Greece_2024-12-05, p. 35">ⓘ</button>
- The document analyzes primary budget balance figures, reporting positive balances projected for 2025-2027. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Italy_2026-04-23, p. 12" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Italy_2026-04-23, p. 12">ⓘ</button>
- Fiscal variables, such as public debt and budget balances, are assessed as a share of GNI* to provide a better assessment of the fiscal situation, removing globalization-related distortions. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Ireland_2025-02-12, p. 17" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Ireland_2025-02-12, p. 17">ⓘ</button>
- The document analyzes the underlying general government fiscal balance, noting a deterioration driven by pension benefit increases and public wage growth. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Lithuania_2025-03-28, p. 28" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Lithuania_2025-03-28, p. 28">ⓘ</button>
- The document analyzes the underlying government primary financial balance, projecting an increase in the structural fiscal deficit. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Latvia_2026-06-12, p. 20" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Latvia_2026-06-12, p. 20">ⓘ</button>
- The OECD analyzes primary balance trajectories implicitly through debt sustainability projections, highlighting the need for fiscal consolidation to offset aging costs. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Luxembourg_2025-04-28, p. 27-28" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Luxembourg_2025-04-28, p. 27-28">ⓘ</button>
- The OECD recommends adopting a national net spending rule to anchor fiscal policy, replacing the obsolete EU-mandated medium-term objective. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Luxembourg_2025-04-28, p. 31, p. 46" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Luxembourg_2025-04-28, p. 31, p. 46">ⓘ</button>
- The survey evaluates fiscal sustainability through stylised debt scenarios, projecting debt-to-GDP ratios under different policy assumptions, including pension reforms and defence spending increases. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Slovenia_2026-06-16, p. 31" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Slovenia_2026-06-16, p. 31">ⓘ</button>
- The analysis relies on Maastricht definition for debt and deficit, as well as OECD calculations for long-term fiscal sustainability. It incorporates scenarios based on AIReF’s projections for aging costs and pension sustainability. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Spain_2025-11-26, p. 46" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Spain_2025-11-26, p. 46">ⓘ</button>
- The OECD uses illustrative simulations to assess fiscal sustainability. It estimates that combining fiscal adjustment with structural reforms boosting employment could reduce the required primary balance improvement from 5.1% of GDP to 2.4% of GDP to bring debt to 40% of GDP within two decades. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Slovakia_2026-06-25, p. 28-29" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Slovakia_2026-06-25, p. 28-29">ⓘ</button>

### [Post-Programme Surveillance Report](../document-types/post-programme-surveillance-report.qmd)

- Fiscal assessments use the Commission’s Spring 2026 Economic Forecast and the Debt Sustainability Monitor 2025. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/post-programme/Post-Programme-Surveillance-Spring-2026_2026-06-03, p. 2, p. 5, p. 10, p. 15, p. 18" aria-label="Source: ec/post-programme/Post-Programme-Surveillance-Spring-2026_2026-06-03, p. 2, p. 5, p. 10, p. 15, p. 18">ⓘ</button>

## Institutions and Data Sources

- **[European Commission](../institutions/european-commission.qmd)**: The issuer of the report. It provides economic forecasts, assesses country-specific recommendations, and monitors compliance with EU fiscal frameworks. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/country-reports/Croatia_2026-06-03, p. 1, p. 35, p. 42" aria-label="Source: ec/country-reports/Croatia_2026-06-03, p. 1, p. 35, p. 42">ⓘ</button>

- **[Eurostat](../institutions/eurostat.qmd)**: Provided data on general government deficit, debt, and defense expenditure used in the Commission’s assessments. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/recommendations/Latvia_2026-06-03, p. 3-4" aria-label="Source: ec/recommendations/Latvia_2026-06-03, p. 3-4">ⓘ</button>

- **[Eurostat](../institutions/eurostat.qmd)**: Provided data on general government deficit, debt, and defence expenditure used in the assessment. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/recommendations/Malta_2026-06-03, p. 4" aria-label="Source: ec/recommendations/Malta_2026-06-03, p. 4">ⓘ</button>

- **[Eurostat](../institutions/eurostat.qmd)**: Provided data on government deficit, debt, and defense expenditure used in the assessment. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/recommendations/Slovakia_2026-06-03, p. 5" aria-label="Source: ec/recommendations/Slovakia_2026-06-03, p. 5">ⓘ</button>

- **[European Commission](../institutions/european-commission.qmd)**: Issued the recommendation for the Council Recommendation. Activated the national escape clause for [Slovenia](../countries/slovenia.qmd) allowing deviation from expenditure limits. - **[Eurostat](../institutions/eurostat.qmd)**: Provided data on [Slovenia](../countries/slovenia.qmd)'s general government deficit, debt, and defence expenditure <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/recommendations/Slovenia_2026-06-03, p. 4" aria-label="Source: ec/recommendations/Slovenia_2026-06-03, p. 4">ⓘ</button>.
- **[European Commission](../institutions/european-commission.qmd)**: The [European Commission](../institutions/european-commission.qmd) issues Country-Specific Recommendations and assesses [Belgium](../countries/belgium.qmd)’s compliance with EU fiscal rules. It identified Spain as not requiring an in-depth review in the 2026 Alert Mechanism Report. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/recommendations/Spain_2026-06-03, p. 1-3" aria-label="Source: ec/recommendations/Spain_2026-06-03, p. 1-3">ⓘ</button>

- **[OECD](../institutions/oecd.qmd)**: The Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development reported that a large share of Spanish firms, notably small and medium-sized enterprises, cite lack of available financing as a considerable long-term barrier to investment. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/recommendations/Spain_2026-06-03, p. 8" aria-label="Source: ec/recommendations/Spain_2026-06-03, p. 8">ⓘ</button>
- **[European Commission](../institutions/european-commission.qmd)**: The European Commission opened an excessive deficit procedure for Austria in July 2025. - **[Eurostat](../institutions/eurostat.qmd)**: Data on GDP, inflation, and government debt are sourced from Eurostat and national accounts, with revisions noted for 2021–2024. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Austria_2026-03-19, p. 28" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Austria_2026-03-19, p. 28">ⓘ</button>
- **[European Investment Bank](../institutions/european-investment-bank.qmd)**: The European Investment Fund is mentioned as a potential partner in supporting Austria’s venture capital market through public financial institutions. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Austria_2026-03-19, p. 81" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Austria_2026-03-19, p. 81">ⓘ</button>

- **[OECD](../institutions/oecd.qmd)**: The [OECD](../institutions/oecd.qmd) provides macroeconomic forecasts, debt sustainability simulations, and policy recommendations. - **[European Commission](../institutions/european-commission.qmd)**: The document references [European Commission](../institutions/european-commission.qmd) data and policies, such as the European Union fiscal framework and the European Union's Restoration Regulation, which impact Finnish fiscal and environmental policy. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Finland_2025-05-23, p. 116" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Finland_2025-05-23, p. 116">ⓘ</button>
- **[European Commission](../institutions/european-commission.qmd)**: The [European Commission](../institutions/european-commission.qmd) is referenced regarding the EU fiscal framework, providing "technical information" for Croatia's fiscal plan. - **[European Commission](../institutions/european-commission.qmd)**: [European Commission](../institutions/european-commission.qmd) projections are used to estimate the evolution of ageing-related costs in debt sustainability scenarios. - **[International Monetary Fund](../institutions/international-monetary-fund.qmd)**: Stress tests conducted under the [International Monetary Fund](../institutions/international-monetary-fund.qmd)’s 2025 Financial Sector Assessment Program indicate that French banks and insurance companies would remain resilient under severe adverse scenarios. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/France_2026-06-30, p. 19" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/France_2026-06-30, p. 19">ⓘ</button>
- **[OECD](../institutions/oecd.qmd)**: The [OECD](../institutions/oecd.qmd) cites the [European Commission](../institutions/european-commission.qmd)’s Ageing Report, which projects a decline in ageing-related expenditures in Greece compared to the European average. - **[International Monetary Fund](../institutions/international-monetary-fund.qmd)**: The document references [International Monetary Fund](../institutions/international-monetary-fund.qmd) analyses, which broadly align with the [OECD](../institutions/oecd.qmd)’s debt sustainability simulations. - **[Eurostat](../institutions/eurostat.qmd)**: The [OECD](../institutions/oecd.qmd) uses data from [Eurostat](../institutions/eurostat.qmd) for employment rates, unemployment, and other macroeconomic indicators. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Greece_2024-12-05, p. 25" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Greece_2024-12-05, p. 25">ⓘ</button>
- **[European Investment Bank](../institutions/european-investment-bank.qmd)**: The [OECD](../institutions/oecd.qmd) cites [European Investment Bank](../institutions/european-investment-bank.qmd) surveys on regulatory burdens and investment obstacles, noting that perceived burdens in Greece remain high. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Greece_2024-12-05, p. 96" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Greece_2024-12-05, p. 96">ⓘ</button>
- **[European Stability Mechanism](../institutions/european-stability-mechanism.qmd)**: The document mentions that improvements in the banking sector’s resilience, noted by the [European Stability Mechanism](../institutions/european-stability-mechanism.qmd), contributed to Greece’s sovereign credit rating upgrade. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Greece_2024-12-05, p. 21" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Greece_2024-12-05, p. 21">ⓘ</button>
- **[Council of the EU](../institutions/council-of-the-eu.qmd)**: The [OECD](../institutions/oecd.qmd) references the newly adopted EU fiscal rules by the [Council of the EU](../institutions/council-of-the-eu.qmd), noting that Greece’s projected debt decline ensures compliance with these rules. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Greece_2024-12-05, p. 32" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Greece_2024-12-05, p. 32">ⓘ</button>
- **[OECD](../institutions/oecd.qmd)**: The document analyzes debt sustainability under alternative fiscal and structural policy scenarios, assuming a long-term interest rate stabilizing at 4.2% and a weighted average interest rate of 3.2%. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Italy_2026-04-23, p. 40" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Italy_2026-04-23, p. 40">ⓘ</button>
- **[European Commission](../institutions/european-commission.qmd)**: The [OECD](../institutions/oecd.qmd) notes that [Italy](../countries/italy.qmd)'s MTFSP aligns with commitments under the revised EU fiscal rules approved by the [European Commission](../institutions/european-commission.qmd). - **[International Monetary Fund](../institutions/international-monetary-fund.qmd)**: Data from the [International Monetary Fund](../institutions/international-monetary-fund.qmd) is cited for Financial Soundness Indicators regarding banking system vulnerabilities. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Italy_2026-04-23, p. 29" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Italy_2026-04-23, p. 29">ⓘ</button>

- **[International Monetary Fund](../institutions/international-monetary-fund.qmd)**: The survey cites International Monetary Fund Article IV consultations and selected issues reports regarding Ireland, particularly concerning financial stability risks and non-bank financial institutions. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Ireland_2025-02-12, p. 20" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Ireland_2025-02-12, p. 20">ⓘ</button>
- **[OECD](../institutions/oecd.qmd)**: The OECD projects the general government balance and underlying fiscal balance, highlighting the need for fiscal adjustment to address ageing-related costs. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Lithuania_2025-03-28, p. 28" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Lithuania_2025-03-28, p. 28">ⓘ</button>
- **[European Commission](../institutions/european-commission.qmd)**: The OECD cites the [European Commission](../institutions/european-commission.qmd)'s 2024 Ageing Report for projections of ageing-related expenditure, which indicate a significant increase between 2022 and 2070. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Lithuania_2025-03-28, p. 13" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Lithuania_2025-03-28, p. 13">ⓘ</button>
- **[OECD](../institutions/oecd.qmd)**: The document analyzes the underlying government primary financial balance, projecting an increase in the structural fiscal deficit. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Latvia_2026-06-12, p. 20" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Latvia_2026-06-12, p. 20">ⓘ</button>
- **[European Commission](../institutions/european-commission.qmd)**: The document references the European Commission's assessment of Latvia's National Energy and Climate Plan and its data on cohesion policy funding absorption. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Latvia_2026-06-12, p. 53" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Latvia_2026-06-12, p. 53">ⓘ</button>
- **[European Central Bank](../institutions/european-central-bank.qmd)**: The European Central Bank is mentioned regarding the monitoring of macroprudential stance and banking sector profitability. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Latvia_2026-06-12, p. 25" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Latvia_2026-06-12, p. 25">ⓘ</button>
- **[European Investment Bank](../institutions/european-investment-bank.qmd)**: The European Investment Bank is cited in the context of surveying business constraints. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Latvia_2026-06-12, p. 86" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Latvia_2026-06-12, p. 86">ⓘ</button>
- **[International Monetary Fund](../institutions/international-monetary-fund.qmd)**: The International Monetary Fund is referenced regarding financial soundness indicators and stress tests. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Latvia_2026-06-12, p. 25" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Latvia_2026-06-12, p. 25">ⓘ</button>
- **[Eurostat](../institutions/eurostat.qmd)**: Eurostat data is used for life expectancy, healthy life years, and unit labor cost comparisons. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Latvia_2026-06-12, p. 11" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Latvia_2026-06-12, p. 11">ⓘ</button>
- **[European Commission](../institutions/european-commission.qmd)**: The [European Commission](../institutions/european-commission.qmd) publishes the Debt Sustainability Monitor as part of its economic surveillance duties. The document serves as input for the European Semester and the reformed EU fiscal framework. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 11, p. 12" aria-label="Source: ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 11, p. 12">ⓘ</button>
- **[European Central Bank](../institutions/european-central-bank.qmd)**: The [European Central Bank](../institutions/european-central-bank.qmd)'s composite indicator of systemic sovereign stress (SovCISS) is used to monitor short-term sovereign risk. The [European Central Bank](../institutions/european-central-bank.qmd)'s policy rates and asset purchase programs are noted in the context of financing conditions and debt holder composition. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 21, p. 23, p. 74" aria-label="Source: ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 21, p. 23, p. 74">ⓘ</button>
- **[Eurostat](../institutions/eurostat.qmd)**: [Eurostat](../institutions/eurostat.qmd) data is used for government debt statistics, including the Maastricht definition and non-EDP liabilities. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 79, p. 81" aria-label="Source: ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 79, p. 81">ⓘ</button>
- **[European Commission](../institutions/european-commission.qmd)**: The document is issued by the European Commission and uses its autumn forecast and debt sustainability analysis (DSA) methodology. The Commission calculates S1 and S2 indicators and defines risk categories. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 222-303" aria-label="Source: ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 222-303">ⓘ</button>
- **[Eurostat](../institutions/eurostat.qmd)**: Eurostat is the source for quarterly data used in stochastic projections, including primary balance, interest rates, and GDP growth. It also provides data on government debt by instrument and maturity. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 273, p. 291-292" aria-label="Source: ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 273, p. 291-292">ⓘ</button>
- **[European Central Bank](../institutions/european-central-bank.qmd)**: The European Central Bank provides data on government debt securities by maturity, interest rates, and bank sector indicators such as non-performing loans and capital ratios. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 291-292" aria-label="Source: ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 291-292">ⓘ</button>
- **[European Commission](../institutions/european-commission.qmd)**: Published the Debt Sustainability Monitor 2025. Assessed the fiscal sustainability condition for activating the national escape clause (NEC) for 16 Member States. Calculated prior guidance and assessed plausibility of adjustment paths in medium-term plans. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 112" aria-label="Source: ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 112">ⓘ</button>
- **[Council of the EU](../institutions/council-of-the-eu.qmd)**: Endorsed net expenditure paths for Member States. Activated the NEC based on Commission recommendations. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 112" aria-label="Source: ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 112">ⓘ</button>
- **[European Central Bank](../institutions/european-central-bank.qmd)**: Participates in the Debt Sustainability Analysis (DSA) working group. Its composite indicator of systemic sovereign stress (SovCISS) is referenced in market risk charts. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 118" aria-label="Source: ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 118">ⓘ</button>
- **[European Fiscal Board](../institutions/european-fiscal-board.qmd)**: Invited as an observer to the DSA working group. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 118" aria-label="Source: ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 118">ⓘ</button>
- **[European Stability Mechanism](../institutions/european-stability-mechanism.qmd)**: Invited as an observer to the DSA working group. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 118" aria-label="Source: ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 118">ⓘ</button>
- **[European Commission](../institutions/european-commission.qmd)**: The document is prepared by the Directorate-General for Economic and Financial Affairs under the responsibility of Maarten Verwey and João Nogueira Martins. It presents the Spring 2026 European Economic Forecast. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/forecast/Spring-2026-Economic-Forecast_2026-05-21, p. 201" aria-label="Source: ec/forecast/Spring-2026-Economic-Forecast_2026-05-21, p. 201">ⓘ</button>

- **[OECD](../institutions/oecd.qmd)**: The [OECD](../institutions/oecd.qmd) suggests enhancing the mandate of the national fiscal council to include long-term debt sustainability assessments and to monitor compliance with the new national fiscal rule <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Luxembourg_2025-04-28, p. 31, p. 46" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Luxembourg_2025-04-28, p. 31, p. 46">ⓘ</button>
- **[European Commission](../institutions/european-commission.qmd)**: The [European Commission](../institutions/european-commission.qmd) assessed [Slovenia](../countries/slovenia.qmd)'s 2026 Draft Budgetary Plan as at risk of non-compliance with the EU fiscal framework but noted that deviations were within allowed flexibility margins. The Commission also confirmed the implementation status of the [Slovenia](../countries/slovenia.qmd)n Recovery and Resilience Plan. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Slovenia_2026-06-16, p. 30" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Slovenia_2026-06-16, p. 30">ⓘ</button>
- **[European Central Bank](../institutions/european-central-bank.qmd)**: The [European Central Bank](../institutions/european-central-bank.qmd) implemented a policy rate cut in June 2025, leading to decreasing interest rates on loans and deposits in [Slovenia](../countries/slovenia.qmd). The Bank of Slovenia (national central bank) adjusted macroprudential tools, such as increasing the countercyclical capital buffer. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Slovenia_2026-06-16, p. 25" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Slovenia_2026-06-16, p. 25">ⓘ</button>
- **[International Monetary Fund](../institutions/international-monetary-fund.qmd)**: The [International Monetary Fund](../institutions/international-monetary-fund.qmd) is cited regarding the assessment of active labour market policies and the fiscal impact of pension reforms. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Slovenia_2026-06-16, p. 21" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Slovenia_2026-06-16, p. 21">ⓘ</button>
- **[European Commission](../institutions/european-commission.qmd)**: The document references the EU Recovery and Resilience Plan (RRP) funds, which have supported investment and growth. The European Commission has endorsed Spain’s medium-term fiscal plan. The document also notes the alignment of national fiscal rules with the new EU fiscal framework overseen by the Commission <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Spain_2025-11-26, p. 30, p. 45" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Spain_2025-11-26, p. 30, p. 45">ⓘ</button>.
- **[European Central Bank](../institutions/european-central-bank.qmd)**: The Bank of Spain has introduced a countercyclical capital buffer (CCyB) of 0.5%, increasing to 1%, aligning with European Central Bank guidance on climate risk and financial stability. The ECB’s projections on the impact of RRP funds on potential growth are cited <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Spain_2025-11-26, p. 30, p. 35" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Spain_2025-11-26, p. 30, p. 35">ⓘ</button>.
- **[International Monetary Fund](../institutions/international-monetary-fund.qmd)**: The document cites IMF stress tests indicating the banking sector is well-positioned to withstand shocks. It also references IMF Article IV consultations regarding fiscal policy and environmental taxation <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Spain_2025-11-26, p. 34, p. 51" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Spain_2025-11-26, p. 34, p. 51">ⓘ</button>.
- **[European Investment Bank](../institutions/european-investment-bank.qmd)**: The document mentions the European Investment Bank’s role in supporting infrastructure and green transition projects, although specific financial flows are not detailed in the extracted figures <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Spain_2025-11-26, p. 30" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Spain_2025-11-26, p. 30">ⓘ</button>.
- **[World Bank](../institutions/world-bank.qmd)**: The World Bank’s Worldwide Governance Indicators are cited in the context of corruption and public procurement challenges in Spain <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Spain_2025-11-26, p. 54" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Spain_2025-11-26, p. 54">ⓘ</button>.
- **[European Commission](../institutions/european-commission.qmd)**: The European Commission notified a reversal of a milestone in April 2024 regarding the approval of national expenditure ceilings under the EU Recovery and Resilience Plan. The Commission also issued Country-Specific Recommendations in 2025, highlighting weaknesses in investment planning and transparency <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Slovakia_2026-06-25, p. 48, 88" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Slovakia_2026-06-25, p. 48, 88">ⓘ</button>.
- **[European Investment Bank](../institutions/european-investment-bank.qmd)**: The European Investment Bank (EIB) Investment Survey data are cited to show that lack of skilled staff is a pressing obstacle for investment in Slovakia. The EIB also notes that few companies report financing constraints as a major obstacle to investment <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Slovakia_2026-06-25, p. 82, 90" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Slovakia_2026-06-25, p. 82, 90">ⓘ</button>.
- **[International Monetary Fund](../institutions/international-monetary-fund.qmd)**: The International Monetary Fund (IMF) conducted stress tests in 2024, concluding that the Slovak banking sector possesses strong capacity to absorb shocks. The IMF’s Article IV Consultation Staff Report is also cited regarding pension reforms <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Slovakia_2026-06-25, p. 25, 30" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Slovakia_2026-06-25, p. 25, 30">ⓘ</button>.
- **[Eurostat](../institutions/eurostat.qmd)**: Eurostat data are used to track AI adoption among enterprises, showing that 18% of Slovak enterprises used AI in 2025.
